previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with cough, wheezing, and low-grade fevers during cycle 14 of lenalidomide/bortezomib/dexamethasone for relapsed multiple myeloma. He had a history of hypogammaglobulinemia and recent transfusion. Initial evaluation showed no acute findings on chest X-ray, negative respiratory viral panel, and inconclusive sputum culture. He was treated with levofloxacin for suspected bronchitis and received IV immunoglobulin for immune support. His respiratory symptoms improved with bronchodilators, and he remained afebrile. Blood cultures remained negative at discharge. He was discharged home on a short course of antibiotics and new inhalers for ongoing wheezing, with plans to resume oncology treatment after recovery.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained through the thorax from
the thoracic inlet to the lung bases without contrast.  Reformatted coronal,
sagittal, and thin slice axial images, were submitted to PACS and reviewed.

Total DLP (Body) = 809 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest ___.

FINDINGS: 

Optimal evaluation of organ pathology and vasculature is limited without the
benefit of intravenous contrast.

CT THORAX:  On the mediastinal windows, The thyroid is unremarkable.  The
imaged esophagus is within normal limits.  The thoracic aorta is normal in
caliber without evidence of intramural hematoma.  The pulmonary artery is
unremarkable within the limitation of noncontrast technique.  Mild
calcification of the LAD coronary artery is seen.  The imaged heart and
pericardium are within normal limits.  There is no evidence of mediastinal,
hilar, axillary, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

Lung windows demonstrate airways which are patent to subsegmental levels. 
There are bilateral, diffuse pulmonary nodules measuring up to 3 mm(for
example see series 4, image 117) which appear in a random distribution. 
Nodules uniformly demonstrate surrounding halo of ground-glass haze.  These
are new since chest CT from ___.  Although nonspecific, in the
setting of immunosuppression these findings are concerning for early acute
infection, especially involving fungal organisms.  The differential also
includes multifocal metastases with surrounding hemorrhage; although this
appearance is less common in a patient with known multiple myeloma.  There is
no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.

Colonic diverticulosis is noted in the partially imaged colon otherwise, the
visualized upper abdominal solid and hollow viscous organs are unremarkable.

MUSCULOSKELETAL:  There is evidence of callus formation around multiple old
left posterior rib fractures.  A chronic appearing Schmorl's node is seen in
involving the superior endplate of the T12 vertebral body.  A well corticated
bony fragment is noted anterior to the inferior margin of the right scapula,
likely an old fracture.  There are diffuse sclerotic foci within this right
scapula, likely related to the patient's known multiple myeloma.  Otherwise,
there is mild background thoracic spine degenerative change.  Alignment is
normal.  No concerning focal lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions are
identified.

IMPRESSION:


1. Diffuse, multifocal randomly distributed pulmonary nodules measuring up to
3 mm with surrounding ground-glass haze/halo, new since the prior chest CT
dated ___.  In the setting of immunosuppression, findings are
concerning for early acute infection, especially involving fungal organisms. 
Differential includes multifocal metastases with surrounding hemorrhage,
although this appearance is less common in a patient with known multiple
myeloma.
2. Colonic diverticulosis.
3. Multiple old healed fractures involving the left posterior ribs and right
inferior scapula.
